headline: High-risk shared-write and prompt-injection pathways exist; no direct evidence of a documented pairwise bridge, so interaction risk is inferred from profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write files, use MCP, and run browsers; nuwa-skill has no documented isolation or parsing safeguards. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge could let ECC-originated content influence nuwa-skill, but the exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty is escalated to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, clipboard, or MCP endpoint, then attacker-controlled content from one can reach the other.
IF nuwa-skill parses external text as instructions, then injected directives can be executed.
mitigations: Separate working directories and MCP roots for each agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of files produced by the other agent.
Require a human review step before copying outputs between agents.
Turn off browser-driven content ingestion for untrusted pages.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, git history, documentation, and security findings, while nuwa-skill has no documented data classes or storage controls. If they share a workspace, ECC can expose sensitive local artifacts to nuwa-skill outputs; the lack of explicit isolation makes this a default-configuration concern, not merely unusual setup.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace, then files touched by ECC can be read into nuwa-skill workflows.
IF nuwa-skill forwards its context to a third-party backend, then shared artifacts may be exfiltrated.
mitigations: Use separate repositories and home directories.
Restrict shared folders to non-sensitive files only.
Remove secrets from ECC-managed paths before handoff.
Audit which files each agent can read in the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has filesystem write, git-state modification, and subprocess/network capabilities; nuwa-skill at least has allowlisted network egress. Even without explicit write permissions on B, overlapping mutable-resource access is plausible through shared repos or APIs, and the missing concurrency details mean the safer medium severity is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository or mutable workspace, then concurrent edits can conflict.
IF both agents write to the same external service through allowlisted network access, then state races can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or repositories.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same mutable resource.
Review and merge changes manually after each run.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and modify code, docs, and security findings, and nuwa-skill is a research-oriented agent with no documented verification barrier. If nuwa-skill consumes ECC output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream research or actions; the pair lacks evidence of a built-in validation step, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill treats ECC-produced text as authoritative, then incorrect facts can propagate.
IF ECC outputs are used as inputs to downstream actions without verification, then mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require explicit source checking before reuse of ECC outputs.
Insert a human verification step for factual claims.
Keep ECC outputs as drafts, not final artifacts.
Compare outputs against primary sources before acting.
requires-engineering: add automated validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles security findings, git history, and session data, but nuwa-skill has no documented regulated-data handling or residency constraints. There is no direct evidence of a residency or certification mismatch between the pair, so compliance risk is limited to cautious low severity rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ECC-managed files and then shared with nuwa-skill, then policy review is required.
IF either agent is used on data subject to retention rules, then operator controls must be checked.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Document which data classes each agent may touch.
Set short retention for ECC session artifacts.
Review vendor and residency terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing controls.
